excerpt: GitCafe repositories work with any Git client over HTTPS or SSH.
Browse files, compare diffs, and leave feedback alongside the code.
Build on an open pull request. Review each change separately, then merge the stack in order.
`cafe stack submit` pushes each commit after the base as its own branch and opens or reuses one pull request per commit. Run it from your checkout; it works with Git, jj and Sapling.
Landing merges the stack from the bottom up through the pull request you choose.
Bring repositories from GitHub into GitCafe with their issues, pull requests, reviews and comments, and optionally keep both sides in sync.
Import from GitHub and keep code, issues, and pull requests in sync, one way or both.
On the sign-up page, choose **Sync with GitHub** and approve GitCafe on GitHub.
GitHub is optional: repositories created in GitCafe need no GitHub account.
It signs you in, sets up Git credentials, and manages repositories, pull requests, stacks, issues and more from the terminal.
Add agent skills to give your coding assistant the same workflow.
`--json` prints structured output; progress and errors go to stderr. `--no-input` fails instead of prompting; `--yes` confirms destructive actions.
`cafe api <path>` sends an authenticated request to any REST API endpoint.
The same description is available as OpenAPI 3.1 JSON for code generators
If the response is lost, send the same request with the same `requestId` again: you get the original result instead of a second operation.
A webhook sends a signed HTTPS request to your server when something happens in a repository or organization, such as a push, a new issue or a merged pull request.
GitCafe shows Buildkite builds on a repository's **CI** tab and as checks on pull requests.
For a repository synchronized with GitHub, you can publish each pipeline's results to GitHub as checks.
A ruleset protects matching branches or tags: it can require pull requests, reviews and passing checks, or block deletion and force pushes.
**Evaluate**: the rules only produce warnings, so you can try them first.
**Code owners**: each changed path needs approval from one of its owners in `CODEOWNERS`
A personal access token lets scripts, CI jobs and tools use the REST API or Git over HTTPS as you, with only the permissions you grant.
GitCafe runs an MCP server at `https://git.cafe/mcp`, so AI tools such as Claude and ChatGPT can read repositories and, with your approval, work on issues and pull requests.
Without connecting an account, its read tools work on public repositories: code, branches and tags, issues, pull requests, reviews and CI results.
Every guide, and most repository pages, can be read as Markdown. This is handy for scripts, coding agents and anything that prefers text to HTML.
A repository's `/<owner>/<repo>/llms.txt` gives an overview of that repository.
In a browser that supports WebMCP, GitCafe pages offer the MCP server's tools to the browser's agent.
Mirror a branch with another Git server
Track work with issues, pin and lock, labels and milestones.
Read a repository's commit history, inspect a single commit, and see who last changed each line of a file.
Private repositories are free during the public beta; paid plans add higher limits.
Your new account also gets the SSH and GPG keys on your GitHub profile, with the default SSH access; keys GitCafe cannot use are skipped.
GitHub Actions results arrive as checks.
offers **Land**, **Restack**, **Unstack** and **Close stack** with the live progress of the latest landing and restack.
Manage repositories, issues, and pull requests with the Cafe CLI.
The button next to an issue or pull request number hands it to a coding agent. Its menu lists Amp, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode and T3 Code
Choose the repository access: **All repositories you can access** (the default...) or **Only select repositories…**
